rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī reads the verse as accepting permission from anyone, including a child, woman, slave, or non-Muslim; permission need not meet testimony’s qualifications.
rows.anchor: ظاهر الآية يقتضي قبول الإذن مطلقا سواء كان الآذان صبيا أو امرأة أو عبدا أو ذميا فإنه لا يعتبر في هذا الإذن صفات الشهادة

rows.speaker: عطاء بن يسار
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ b. Yasār reports that a man asked the Prophet whether he should seek permission to enter upon his sister; the Prophet said yes and asked whether he would want to see her naked.
rows.anchor: عن عطاء بن يسار : ( أن رجلا سأل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال أستأذن على أختي ؟ فقال النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام نعم أتحب أن تراها عريانة )

rows.speaker: حذيفة
rows.claim: A man asked Ḥudhayfa whether to seek permission before entering upon his sister; Ḥudhayfa warned that without permission he might see something distressing.
rows.anchor: وسأل رجل حذيفة أستأذن على أختي ، فقال إن لم تستأذن عليها رأيت ما يسوؤك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says Ibn ʿAbbās answered yes when asked about seeking permission to enter upon and provide for a sister, citing 24:59, which does not distinguish relatives from strangers.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء سألت ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما استأذن على أختي ومن أنفق عليها ؟ قال نعم إن الله تعالى يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī concludes that permission is required before entering upon maḥram relatives, though the matter is easier because some parts of their bodies may lawfully be seen.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن ترك الاستئذان على المحارم وإن كان غير جائز إلا أنه أيسر لجواز النظر إلى شعرها وصدرها وساقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the ban on sudden entry protects someone who may be unclothed, it applies to everyone except wives and owned slave women.
rows.anchor: إن كان لأجل أن ذلك الغير ربما كان منكشف الأعضاء فهذا دخل فيه الكل إلا الزوجات وملك اليمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the concern is interrupting private activity, permission is required before entering anyone’s space, including a wife’s or slave woman’s.
rows.anchor: وإن كان لأجل أنه ربما كان مشتغلا بأمر يكره إطلاع الغير عليه وجب أن يعم في الكل ، حتى لا يكون له أن يدخل على الزوجة والأمة إلا بإذن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says evidentiary exceptions remove the need for permission in emergencies such as fire, a thief’s attack, or a manifest wrong.
rows.anchor: إذا عرض أمر في دار من حريق أو هجوم سارق أو ظهور منكر فهل يجب الاستئذان ؟ الجواب : كل ذلك مستثنى بالدليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salām is a commanded Muslim practice that gives security, is the greeting of Paradise’s people, brings affection, and removes rancor and spite.
rows.anchor: وأما السلام فهو من سنة المسلمين التي أمروا بها ، وأمان للقوم وهو تحية أهل الجنة ومجلبة للمودة وناف للحقد والضغينة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet’s account: after Adam sneezed and praised God, God taught him to greet the angels and said this would be the greeting of Adam and his descendants.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: ʿAlī reports the Prophet listing six Muslim rights: greeting on meeting, answering an invitation, giving private counsel, responding to a sneeze, visiting the sick, and attending a funeral.
rows.anchor: وعن علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports the Prophet urging people to spread salām among themselves if they want rancor removed from their hearts.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عمر قال قال رسول الله عليه الصلاة والسلام

none: A heading on the ruling of gaze followed only by quoted Qurʾān text.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing the polytheists’ denial of prophethood and their doubts, God reports that they mock and belittle the Messenger when they see him, going beyond mere disbelief.
rows.anchor: لما بين مبالغة المشركين في إنكار نبوته وفي إيراد الشبهات في ذلك

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: The author of al-Kashshāf parses the first إن as negative and the second as a lightened form of إنّ; the lām distinguishes them.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) ( إن ) الأولى نافية والثانية مخففة من الثقيلة ، واللام هي الفارقة بينهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response to إذا is an omitted statement: they see you and mock, then say that God sent this person as a messenger; إن يتخذونك interrupts the conditional construction.
rows.anchor: جواب ( إذا ) هو ما أضمر من القول يعني وإذا رأوك مستهزئين قالوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking him as mockery means mocking him; the underlying expression is to make him an object of mockery or a mocked person.
rows.anchor: اتخذوه هزوا في معنى استهزؤا به والأصل اتخذوه موضع هزء أو مهزوءا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī treats their speech as two acts: they ridicule the Messenger, then claim he nearly turned them from their gods unless they stood firm.
rows.anchor: اعلم أن الله تعالى أخبر عن المشركين أنهم متى رأوا الرسول أتوا بنوعين من الأفعال أحدهما أنهم يستهزئون به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If their ridicule targeted his appearance, it was baseless: he was the best-looking among them and did not claim superiority of appearance, but superiority through proof.
rows.anchor: أما الأول فباطل لأنه عليه الصلاة والسلام كان أحسن منهم صورة وخلقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they ridiculed his prophetic qualities, the claim also fails: his distinction was manifest miracles, and they could not challenge his proof; they deserved ridicule, so their reversal displays insolence.
rows.anchor: وأما الثاني فباطل لأنه عليه السلام ادعى التميز عنهم في ظهور المعجز عليه دونهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their fear of being diverted from the idols implies they regarded their worship as true; this refutes the view of the Aṣḥāb al-maʿārif that disbelief occurs only after knowing the proofs, since these people were ignorant yet called unbelievers.
rows.anchor: من هذا الوجه يبطل قول أصحاب المعارف في أنه لا يكفر إلا من يعرف الدلائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their remark that he nearly diverted them shows the Messenger’s strenuous effort to turn them from idolatry through arguments, answers to doubts, and endurance of their abuse.
rows.anchor: يدل هذا القول منهم على جد الرسول عليه السلام واجتهاده في صرفهم عن عبادة الأوثان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their statement indicates that they never answered the Messenger’s proofs with objections; they relied on imitation and stubborn denial and were overwhelmed by his argument.
rows.anchor: وذلك يدل على أن القوم كانوا مقهورين تحت حجته عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their combined remarks make them seem bewildered: mockery fits an ignorant, powerless person, while saying he nearly diverted them attributes learned reasoning and strong proof to him.
rows.anchor: فالقوم لما جمعوا بين هذين الكلامين دل ذلك على أنهم كانوا كالمتحيرين في أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s warning says the punishment will reveal who was farther from the right path; it threatens those who deliberately ignore evidence and refuse reflection.
rows.anchor: سوف يعلمون حين يرون العذاب من أضل سبيلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī explains their rejection as the domination of imitation and desire: they follow whatever inclination urges, whether or not evidence forbids it.
rows.anchor: بلوغ هؤلاء في جهالتهم وإعراضهم عن الدلائل إنما كان لاستيلاء التقليد عليهم

words: وَمَا يَأْتِيهِم مِّن ذِكْرٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ مُحْدَثٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī connects the repeated arrival of new Qurʾānic reminders in 26:5 to God’s ability to compel belief in 26:4: He instead shows mercy by sending revelation again and again, though they persist in denial and mockery.
rows.anchor: من تمام قوله : { إن نشأ ننزل عليهم } ( الشعراء : 4 ) فنبه تعالى على أنه مع قدرته على أن يجعلهم مؤمنين بالإلجاء رحيم بهم من حيث يأتيهم حالا بعد حال بالقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Persistent disbelief calls for stern warning; “they have denied” marks the extreme of rejecting God’s signs, and the coming news of their fate may arrive through worldly punishment, at its sight, or in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: أي بلغوا النهاية / في رد آيات الله تعالى

words: كَمْ أَنۢبَتْنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ زَوْجٍۢ كَرِيمٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A “pair” here means a plant species; “noble” means praiseworthy in its kind, as with a beautiful face, a useful book, or a plant valued for its benefits.
rows.anchor: والزوج هو الصنف ( من النبات ) والكريم صفة لكل ما يرضى ويحمد في بابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation limits “noble pair” to useful plants: vegetation is beneficial or harmful, and God mentions the many useful kinds while leaving harmful ones unmentioned.
rows.anchor: أن النبات على نوعين نافع وضار ، فذكر سبحانه كثرة ما أنبت في الأرض من جميع أصناف النبات النافع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation includes all plants, beneficial and harmful: God calls them all noble to signal that nothing was created without some benefit, even if people overlook it.
rows.anchor: أنه عم جميع النبات نافعه وضاره ووصفهما جميعا بالكرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sign in creation benefits people who reflect and ponder, like the Qurʾān’s description of itself as guidance for the God-conscious; most nevertheless remain disbelievers.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أن في ذلك دلالة لمن يتفكر ويتدبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is named Mighty before Merciful to prevent the inference that He spares them because He cannot punish them; mercy exercised with full power has greater force.
rows.anchor: فإنما قدم ذكر العزيز على ذكر الرحيم لأنه لو لم يقدمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite their disbelief and His ability to punish swiftly, God continues to show mercy through the useful plants He creates and through health, reason, and guidance.
rows.anchor: والمراد أنهم مع كفرهم وقدرة الله على أن يعجل عقابهم لا يترك رحمتهم

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الأشعري
rows.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ashʿarī says Moses heard God’s eternal speech, which is audible yet unlike letters and sounds, just as God Himself is unlike created things.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو الحسن الأشعري : المسموع هو الكلام القديم

rows.speaker: أبو منصور الماتريدي
rows.claim: Abū Manṣūr al-Māturīdī says Moses heard a call made of letters and sounds: vision supports a common cause of existence across visible things, but hearing supplies no parallel proof that every existent thing is audible.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو منصور الماتريدي : الذي سمعه موسى عليه السلام كان نداء من جنس الحروف والأصوات

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilites agree that the heard call consisted of letters and sounds.
rows.anchor: أما المعتزلة فقد اتفقوا على أن ذلك المسموع ما كان إلا حروفا وأصواتا

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilites say the call was miraculous because Moses knew it came from God and was addressed to him; no intermediary was needed. At the start of prophethood he was to summon people to monotheism, then receive legal commands, knowing miracles would appear if demanded.
rows.anchor: فعند هذا قالوا إن ذلك النداء وقع على وجه علم به موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people are called wrongdoers both because their disbelief wrongs themselves and because they wrong the Israelites.
rows.anchor: من وجه ظلمهم أنفسهم بكفرهم ، ومن وجه ظلمهم لبني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The people of Pharaoh” is an explicative apposition to “the wrongdoers”; both expressions designate the same group.
rows.anchor: عطف بيان ، كأن القوم الظالمين وقوم فرعون لفظان يدلان على معنى واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recounting Moses and Abraham, God recounts Noah to console Muhammad for what he faces from his people; Noah preached for 950 years and was still denied.
rows.anchor: قص على محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم خبر موسى وإبراهيم تسلية له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular feminine verb كذبت agrees with قوم because the collective noun is grammatically feminine; its diminutive is قويمة.
rows.anchor: لأن القوم مؤنث وتصغيرها قويمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that although Noah’s people denied Noah, this entails denying the other messengers because the way their prophethood is known does not differ.
rows.anchor: أنهم وإن كذبوا نوحا لكن تكذيبه في المعنى يتضمن تكذيب غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Noah’s people denied all God’s messengers, perhaps because they were unbelieving materialists or Brahmins.
rows.anchor: أن قوم نوح كذبوا بجميع رسل الله تعالى ، إما لأنهم كانوا من الزنادقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah is called their brother because he was one of them; Arab usage addresses a person as “brother of Banū Tamīm” to mean a member of that group.
rows.anchor: فلأنه كان منهم ، من قول العرب يا أخا بني تميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah first warns his people because they accepted their religions through imitation; a person following blindly needs fear to prompt reflection and argument.
rows.anchor: القوم إنما قبلوا تلك الأديان للتقليد والمقلد إذا خوف خاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah reminds them he is a trustworthy messenger, as Muhammad was known among Quraysh: they knew Noah’s honesty before his call, so should not accuse him now.
rows.anchor: وذلك لأنه كان فيهم مشهورا بالأمانة كمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم في قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah says he seeks no payment for his claim to prophethood so they will not suspect him of preaching for personal gain.
rows.anchor: أي على ما أنا فيه من ادعاء الرسالة لئلا يظن به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated call to fear God has distinct grounds: first, they should not disobey God’s messenger; again, they should not disobey a messenger who asks no wage. Rāzī compares this to repeating a rebuke for separate reasons.
rows.anchor: لأنه في الأول أراد ألا تتقون مخالفتي وأنا رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah places fear of God before obedience to himself because piety is the cause of obedience, so the cause precedes its consequence.
rows.anchor: الأمر بطاعته ، لأن تقوى الله علة لطاعته فقدم العلة على المعلول

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf reports that الأرذلون may be parsed as the plural of تابع, like شاهد/أشهاد, or of تبع, like بطل/أبطال.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : وقرى { واتبعك الارذلون } جمع تابع كشاهد وأشهاد أو جمع تبع كبطل وأبطال

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf treats the waw in “and they followed you” as circumstantial; its construction calls for an implied قد after واتبعك.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : وقرى { واتبعك الارذلون } جمع تابع كشاهد وأشهاد أو جمع تبع كبطل وأبطال والواو للحال

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf notes that أرذل has both a regular sound plural and a broken plural, as in “those whom we consider the lowliest” (11:27).
rows.anchor: وقد جمع الأرذل على الصحة وعلى التكسير في قولهم : { الذين هم أراذلنا }

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: The gloss says radhāla means lowness; Noah’s opponents considered his followers low because of their poor lineage and little worldly wealth.
rows.anchor: والرذالة الخسة ، وإنما استرذلوهم لاتضاع نسبهم وقلة نصيبهم من الدنيا

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Rāzī also records an unnamed explanation that the followers were deemed low because they had trades such as weaving and cupping.
rows.anchor: وقيل كانوا من أهل الصناعات الخسيسة كالحياكة والحجامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī dismisses the objection as weak: Noah was sent to all people, so poverty, wealth, or the status of one’s occupation is irrelevant.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن هذه الشبهة في نهاية الركاكة ، لأن نوحا عليه السلام بعث إلى الخلق كافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their accusation implies that Noah’s followers believed without insight, out of desire and hope of gain, as the people say in 11:27 that they followed him at first glance.
rows.anchor: وهذا الكلام يدل على أنهم نسبوهم مع ذلك إلى أنهم لم يؤمنوا عن نظر وبصيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah says only his Lord judges their hidden state; Noah relies on what is outwardly apparent, and adds “if only you understood” because his opponents do not accept this.
rows.anchor: معناه لا نعتبر إلا الظاهر من أمرهم دون ما يخفى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī infers that the people asked Noah to expel the poor believers so they could follow him or draw closer to doing so; Noah refuses because they believe.
rows.anchor: وذلك كالدلالة على أن القوم سألوه إبعادهم لكي يتبعوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah’s mission is to warn those who reject him; anyone who accepts is near to him, while one who rejects is distant, so the mission gives no grounds to expel believers.
rows.anchor: والمراد إني أخوف من كذبني ولم يقبل مني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people threaten to kill Noah by stoning him; at this point he despairs of their salvation and asks God to judge between them.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أنهم خوفوه بأن يقتل بالحجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah is not informing an omniscient God that they denied him; he asks for judgment for God’s sake and religion, since they denied God’s revelation and message.
rows.anchor: وليس الغرض منه إخبار الله تعالى بالتكذيب لعلمه أن عالم الغيب والشهادة أعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here فتح means judge: فتاحة is judgment and الفتاح a judge, metaphorically one who opens what is closed; the following request to be saved shows that the judgment sought is punishment for Noah’s people.
rows.anchor: أي فاحكم بيني وبينهم والفتاحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request to be saved after asking God to judge implies that Noah seeks the people’s punishment; otherwise, the rescue request would not make sense in context.
rows.anchor: ولولا أن المراد إنزال العقوبة لما كان لذكر النجاة بعده معنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says Noah’s story has already been explained at length in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf and Sūrat Hūd.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم القول في قصته مشروحا في سورة الأعراف وسورة هود

none: A story heading followed only by quoted Qurʾān text, without commentary.
A story heading followed only by quoted Qurʾān text, without commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī offers two attachments for “from among the worlds”: it may describe the men as a group distinguished by this act, or the males they chose from among all beings instead of females.
rows.anchor: أي أنتم من جملة العالمين صرتم مخصوصين بهذه الصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “From your wives” may explain what God created or be partitive; on the latter reading, “what He created” means the lawful part of women, and they may have done this with their wives too.
rows.anchor: فيصلح أن يكون تبيينا لما خلق وأن يكون للتبعيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An ʿādī is one who transgresses through injustice.
rows.anchor: والعادي هو المتعدي في ظلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may mean that, in addition to this grave sin, they transgress in all sins, or that this enormity makes them especially deserving of the label transgressors.
rows.anchor: ومعناه أترتكبون هذه المعصية على عظمها بل أنتم قوم عادون في جميع المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat means that Lot would be among those expelled from their town; they may have driven people out in the worst possible conditions.
rows.anchor: أي لتكونن من جملة من أخرجناه من بلدنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qalāʾ means intense hatred, as if the hatred were boiling the heart and liver.
rows.anchor: القلي البغض الشديد ، كأنه بغض يقلي الفؤاد والكبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying “among those who hate” is more emphatic than saying “I hate your act”; it can mean Lot is among those complete in their hatred of them.
rows.anchor: أبلغ من أن يقول إني لعملكم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God saved Lot and his household from the punishment for their deed; the exception of the old woman means her destruction was decreed even though “remaining” was not yet her state at the time of rescue.
rows.anchor: صفة لها كأنه قيل إلا عجوزا غابرة

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: An unnamed report says Lot’s old wife perished with those left in the town when stones rained down on them.
rows.anchor: قيل إنها هلكت مع من خرج من القرية بما أمطر عليهم من الحجارة

words: وَتَذَرُونَ مَا خَلَقَ لَكُم مِّنْ أَزْوَٰجِكُم
rows.speaker: القاضي عبد الجبار
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī ʿAbd al-Jabbār argues against determinism: “leaving” presumes ability to do otherwise; what God created would be imposed rather than left; and attributing transgression to people is incoherent if God creates their acts, as calling someone transgressive for their skin color would be.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي عبد الجبار في ( تفسيره )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī summarizes the free-will argument: unless people originate their own acts, praise, blame, commands, and prohibitions cannot properly apply to them.
rows.anchor: فنقول حاصل هذه الوجوه يرجع إلى أن العبد لو لم يكن موجدا الأفعال نفسه لما توجه المدح والذم والأمر والنهي عليه

words: وَتَذَرُونَ مَا خَلَقَ لَكُم مِّنْ أَزْوَٰجِكُم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī notes that this story’s wording has a special force for the free-will debate beyond the commands, prohibitions, praise, and blame in the stories of Moses, Abraham, and Noah.
rows.anchor: ولهذه الآية في هذا المعنى خاصية أزيد مما ورد من الأمر والنهي والمدح والذم في قصة موسى عليه السلام وإبراهيم ونوح وسائر القصص

words: وَتَذَرُونَ مَا خَلَقَ لَكُم مِّنْ أَزْوَٰجِكُم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī answers that because God knows these acts will occur, their nonoccurrence is impossible: it would turn divine knowledge into ignorance, so commanding people to refrain would demand the impossible.
rows.anchor: أن الله تعالى لما علم وقوع هذه الأشياء فعدمها محال لأن عدمها يستلزم انقلاب العلم جهلا وهو محال

words: وَتَذَرُونَ مَا خَلَقَ لَكُم مِّنْ أَزْوَٰجِكُم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A choice between two possible acts requires a preponderant motive or will; that originated motive needs a cause, and if the human causes it regress is infinite, while if God causes it the result is compulsion.
rows.anchor: القادر لما كان قادرا على الضدين امتنع أن يترجح أحد المقدورين على الآخر إلا لمرجح وهو الداعي أو الإرادة وذلك المرجح محدث فله مؤثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī concludes that these two arguments defeat al-Qāḍī ʿAbd al-Jabbār’s case against determinism.
rows.anchor: فثبت بهذين البرهانين القاطعين سقوط ما قاله والله أعلم
